summary: Gustavo Del Vechio asks on the Adobe Photoshop community forum whether text in a JavaScript (ExtendScript) dialog's statictext or an alert can contain a clickable hyperlink, such as a website or mailto e-mail address. Davide (DBarranca) replies that alerts cannot do this, but a dialog's statictext can get a click event listener that writes and executes a temporary .url shortcut file; he marks this as the correct answer. JJMack suggests writing a local HTML file with a redirect or mailto link and executing it so the default browser opens, and Gustavo and another user thank the responders.
one_line: Forum thread asking whether ExtendScript dialog text or alerts in Photoshop scripts can contain clickable hyperlinks, with workarounds.
key_facts: The thread is titled "Hyperlink in the scripts's UI" on the Adobe Community Photoshop ecosystem discussions board, posted September 13, 2013.
Gustavo Del Vechio asked whether a statictext in a JavaScript dialog or a portion of text in an alert pop-up could be a hyperlink.
Gustavo's example code created a dialog with dlg.add("statictext") containing www.mysite.com and a button whose onClick called alert().
DBarranca (Davide Barranca) replied that as far as he knows it is not possible within an Alert.

DBarranca suggested attaching an eventListener to the dialog's statictext (dlg.myText.addEventListener('click', ...)) that writes a temporary _shortcut.url file with an [InternetShortcut] URL entry and executes it.
DBarranca's shortcut approach calls $.sleep(4000) and then shortcut.remove(), and he described it as "Not very much elegant" but working.
DBarranca's answer was marked as the correct answer and has 0 upvotes.
JJMack, a Community Expert, suggested writing an HTML file to Folder.temp and executing it so the user's default browser opens.
JJMack said the HTML file could include a meta REFRESH redirect to a web site and a mailto link, and could be kept local so no internet connection is required.
JJMack said the script keeps running and is not stopped by the alert when the browser window opens.
Gustavo replied on September 16, 2013 that he would try this approach, thanking Davide and JJMack.
matias.kiviniemi, an Enthusiast, replied on October 03, 2014 that the JJMack suggestion saved his day.
The thread has 4 replies and about 1.2K views, and is filed under the TOPICS category 'Actions and scripting'.
